facts.text: ReadBundleFormat returns the format only when the manifest's format property is a JSON string, and null when it is a number or absent.
ReadBundleFormat catches a JsonException and returns null, so an unparseable manifest reads as a markdown bundle instead of failing.
ReadBundleFormat raises import_unsafe_path, rather than returning null, when manifest.json is a symbolic link.
at: manifest.json is a symbolic link; refusing to read it

facts.text: ReadBundleFormat returns null when the manifest is absent or longer than ImportManifestMaxBytes.
A hidden entry under assets/ that the manifest does not list is skipped as hidden_file_ignored and its subtree is never walked.
RejectUnlistedAssets walks the assets directory only when it exists and is not a link.
A non-hidden entry under assets/ that the manifest does not list raises import_unlisted_file.
at: {relative} is in the bundle directory but not listed

facts.text: OpenRegularFile on Windows opens with FileShare.Read and FileOptions.SequentialScan instead of calling Posix.Open.
OpenRegularFile maps open errno 2 and 20 to import_file_missing.
OpenRegularFile maps errno 40 on Linux and 62 elsewhere, plus errno 31, to import_unsafe_path.
OpenRegularFile disposes the stream and raises import_not_regular_file when the opened handle cannot seek.
ReadManifestDocument reads at most the smaller of the stream length and ImportManifestMaxBytes before parsing.
When ReadAtMost returns null, ReadManifestDocument raises import_unsafe_path for a manifest too large or longer than its file size says.
at: manifest.json is too large to read

facts.text: ReadManifestDocument opens the manifest through OpenRegularFile with a 4096-byte buffer.
ReadJsonlFile raises import_file_mismatch when the data file does not end with a newline.
at: {name} does not end with a newline

facts.text: ReadJsonlFile raises import_line_too_long before buffering a line that exceeds maxLine bytes.
at: is longer than the {maxLine}-byte line limit

facts.text: The line buffer doubles on growth but is capped at maxLine rather than at the doubled size.
ReadJsonlFile raises import_file_missing when the manifest lists a data file that is not in the bundle.
at: manifest.json lists {name} but the file is not in the bundle

facts.text: ReadJsonlFile raises import_unsafe_path for a data file that is a symbolic link or reparse point.
at: is a symbolic link or reparse point; refusing to read it

facts.text: ReadJsonlFile raises import_file_mismatch when the file length on disk differs from the bytes file_stats declares.
ReadJsonlFile raises import_file_mismatch as soon as the stream holds more bytes than file_stats declares.
at: holds more than the {stats.Bytes} bytes file_stats says; stopped reading

facts.text: ReadJsonlFile raises import_file_mismatch when the final byte or line count differs from file_stats.
at: holds {chunkBase} bytes in {lineNumber} lines but file_stats says

facts.text: ReadJsonlFile hashes the whole stream and raises import_file_mismatch when the hex digest differs from file_stats.
After each newline, lineStart is set to the chunk base plus the position just past that newline.
ImportJsonl raises import_bad_manifest unless the manifest root has a files array and a file_stats object.
ImportJsonl parses a data file's number from its name after skipping 8 characters and dropping the last 14.
Data files are read ordered by their parsed file number, not by their order in the manifest.
A line that is not a JSON object with a string type raises import_bad_record.
at: is not a JSON object with a string

facts.text: ImportJsonl raises bundle_has_no_records when the bundle yielded no readable fact lines.
at: the JSONL bundle holds no readable fact lines

facts.text: Two manifest names with the same parsed file number raise import_bad_manifest.
at: more than once (or two names with the same file number)

facts.text: A manifest files entry that is neither a data file name nor an asset path raises import_unlisted_file.
at: which is not a file name a JSONL bundle can contain

facts.text: A dossier jsonl file present in the bundle directory but absent from the manifest raises import_unlisted_file.
A file_stats entry naming something the manifest does not list as a data file raises import_file_mismatch.
at: which manifest.json does not list as a data file

facts.text: A file_stats entry needs non-negative bytes and lines plus a 64-character lowercase sha256, or import_file_mismatch is raised.
at: lacks bytes, lines or a 64-character lowercase sha256

facts.text: A listed data file with no file_stats entry raises import_file_mismatch.
at: but file_stats has no bytes/lines/sha256 for it

facts.text: An empty line in a data file raises import_bad_record.
A subject line without a non-empty id or name is skipped with the reason that it lacks id or name.
at: subject line lacks id or name

facts.text: A subject id that appears on two subject lines raises import_duplicate_id.
A subject line without a kind gets the kind subject.
A fact id claimed by two fact lines raises import_duplicate_id naming both locations.
at: is claimed by two fact lines

facts.text: Each accepted fact line gets an Order value from a counter incremented as lines are read.
An asset line without a sha256 is skipped rather than treated as an error.
An asset record repeating a sha256 with a different path, bytes, mime, data or missing flag raises import_bad_record.
at: repeats asset {sha} with a different path

facts.text: A record whose type is not subject, fact or asset is skipped with an unknown record type skip.
A subject id referenced by a fact but never declared gets created with kind subject and no parent.
Blob restore runs at most once per sha256 because outcomes are memoized in a done dictionary.
The line limit comes from the MaxLineBytes option when it is positive, otherwise from DefaultImportMaxLineBytes.
ImportJsonl raises import_unsafe_path when the manifest is a symbolic link or larger than ImportManifestMaxBytes.
at: manifest.json is a symbolic link or too large to read

facts.text: A repeated asset record is accepted when its path, bytes, mime, data and missing flag all match the first record for that sha256.
A subject line's pin object is stored as canonical JSON produced by CanonicalJson.Write.
Aliases are collected only from array elements that are strings; other element kinds are ignored.
A files entry naming manifest.json itself is skipped instead of treated as a data file or asset.
Hidden-file skips collected from assets/ are added to the import result's skip list before any data file is read.
RestoreJsonlBlob refuses a sha256 that is not 64 lowercase hex characters and reports that as the skip reason.
at: sha256 is not 64 lowercase hex characters

facts.text: An attachment whose bytes have no asset record is not restored, and the attachment row is kept without its blob.
An asset record flagged missing yields no blob and the skip reason says the blob was missing at publish time.
at: the blob was missing when the bundle was published

facts.text: A restored blob is written to BlobRoot joined with the sha256, not to the recorded asset path.
An asset record carrying embedded data is restored from the jsonl line before any file path is considered.
An asset record with neither embedded data nor a path is skipped with a reason naming both.
at: asset record carries neither embedded data nor a path

facts.text: RestoreFileBlob accepts only a path equal to assets/ plus the asset's own sha256, optionally followed by one extension.
A path that is not among the manifest's listed files is skipped rather than read.
at: is not listed in manifest.json files; not read

facts.text: A path whose full form escapes the bundle root is skipped rather than read.
at: resolves outside the bundle; not read

facts.text: An asset file or its directory that is a symbolic link or reparse point is skipped, not read.
at: asset file {path} is a symbolic link or reparse point; not read

facts.text: A freshly copied blob is moved into place only when no blob already exists at the target.
When the asset file holds more than the copy limit, RestoreFileBlob skips it with a reason naming that limit.
at: holds more than the {limit} bytes it should; not read further

facts.text: An import_not_regular_file failure while opening an asset file becomes a skip reason rather than an import error.
RestoreEmbeddedBlob re-opens the data file and seeks to the byte offset pass 1 recorded for the asset line.
An embedded asset whose encoding is not base64 is skipped with the observed encoding in the reason.
An embedded asset whose declared size is negative or above MaxEmbedAssetBytes is not decoded.
Embedded data that contains JSON escapes is refused, as is a line with no data property.
The base64 payload length must match the padded encoding of the declared byte count, else the data is not decoded.
After decoding, the sha256 of the content must equal the recorded sha256 or the blob is not restored.
An embedded blob goes to a temporary file and is moved into place so a crash cannot leave a truncated content-addressed blob.
at: a crash never leaves a truncated content-addressed blob

facts.text: A failure while re-reading the asset line is reported as a skip reason that includes the file and line.
ReadAtMost sizes its buffer as min of the limit and Array.MaxLength so an extreme limit cannot overflow the array size.
When the stream ends before the buffer fills, ReadAtMost resizes the array down to the bytes actually read.
UnixOpenFlags puts linux Arm64, Arm, Armv6 and Ppc64le in one group with a different O_NOFOLLOW bit than the x86-style group.
at: Architecture.Arm64 or Architecture.Arm or Architecture.Armv6 or Architecture.Ppc64le

facts.text: An unrecognised os and architecture pair throws import_unsupported_platform instead of guessing flag values.
CopyAtMost reports whether more input remained by reading one further byte after the copy limit is reached.
AssetCopyLimit treats a negative declared size as unknown and still never copies past the opened handle length.
